summary: This is the Usage page of the Crazyswarm2 ROS 2 documentation for controlling Crazyflie drones. It explains sourcing the ROS 2 workspace, restricting ROS to the local machine on shared networks, and the layout of configuration files, especially crazyflies.yaml with robot entries, robot_types and an 'all' section. It also covers running simulation, teleoperation with an XBox controller, Python scripts, and the swarm management GUI.
one_line: Usage guide for Crazyswarm2 covering ROS 2 configuration files, simulation, teleoperation, Python scripts and swarm management for Crazyflie drones.
key_facts: Users must source their ROS 2 workspace in each terminal with '. install/local_setup.bash' before using it.
On a shared network, users can set ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1 and a unique ROS_DOMAIN_ID between 0 and 101 to avoid controlling other robots.
All configuration files are located in crazyflie/config.
The crazyflies.yaml file sets up everything related to the robots, while server.yaml covers the server, motion_capture.yaml covers the motion capture package, and teleop.yaml covers remote controls.
Each crazyflie should have a unique URI, which can be changed in Bitcraze's CFclient.
In the example configuration, the robot cf231 uses URI radio://0/80/2M/E7E7E7E7E7 with type cf21 and is enabled.
The cf21 robot type sets battery voltage_warning to 3.8 V and voltage_critical to 3.7 V.
The 'all' field in crazyflies.yaml applies parameters or logging to all connected crazyflies, and the server gives it the lowest priority.
The firmware_params example sets stabilizer estimator to 2 (kalman) and controller to 2 (mellinger).
Simulation uses the firmware code as software-in-the-loop and can optionally include robot dynamics; its configuration can be changed in server.yaml.
The command 'ros2 launch crazyflie_examples launch.py script:=hello_world backend:=sim' runs the simulation shorthand for hello_world.
The teleoperation controller assumes an XBox controller, whose button mapping can be changed in teleop.yaml.
Teleoperation supports attitude-control and position-control modes, where position control can be assisted by any localization system.
The swarm management tool is a ROS node and web-based GUI that shows drone location in a 3D window and status and log messages in a lower pane.
